newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court approves HLL share issue to Unilever.
newsitem.headline: Indian court approves HLL share issue to Unilever.

text.p: An Indian court on Monday ratified an agreement between the country's central bank and two Indian units of Unilever Plc for a preferential allotment of shares to the UK-based firm, Hindustan Lever Ltd (HLL) said in a statement.
Unilever units HLL, Pond's and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) recently reached an out of court settlement over the pricing of the preferential issue, four years after the initial issue of shares.
Accordingly 2,984,347 equity shares of HLL, allotted on a preferential basis to Unilever, will be priced at 357 rupees a share.

Pond's will resubmit its application to the RBI for preferential allotment of 931,000 Unilever shares to Unilever at 620 rupees a share. The preferential allotment will raise Unilever's equity in Pond's to 51 percent from 47.7 percent.
The division bench of the Bombay High Court took on record the out of court settlement between the central bank and the two Unilever subsidiaries and disposed of the petitions, HLL said.
The firm said in the statement the preferential allotment by Hind Lever Chemicals Ltd -- previously known as Stepan Chemicals Ltd -- had been withdrawn.
